name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum: long the confirmed 2026 leadership complexes — AI semiconductors (SMH core plus AMAT and NVDA), AI power (GEV) and oil-shock E&P (XOP) — against the two cleanest measured losers, long-duration Treasuries (TLT) and rate-killed homebuilders (ITB).
reassessment_note: One-leg rotation only, after re-measuring momentum from Yahoo daily closes (which match the packet marks to the cent). The book is down about 4.4% over five sessions, almost all of it from the semis pullback (SMH -4.3% over 5d, AMAT -6.1%), but on a 6-month lookback the ranking the book is built on still holds: SMH +38%, AMAT +27%, NVDA +22%, XOP +14%, XLE +14% against TLT -10%, ITB -10%, SPY +15%. A one-week pullback in a leader is not a signal for a 6-month momentum book, and every stop is far from being hit (worst is AMAT at -6.5% against a -15% stop). AVGO is the exception: -2.7% over 6m and -5.9% over 3m, so by the book's own rule it is a laggard and should not be held as a leader. I am swapping its 8% into NVDA, the semi with the strongest 3m/6m trend that the book does not already hold through a single name. GEV stays: its 6m momentum is weak (+1.4%), but it has rebounded 8.7% in a month and is +1.5% on the leg, so I will reassess it next week rather than churn it. Rates context from search: the 10y reached 5.34% on 10-05 (highest since 2002) and eased toward about 5.17% by week's end, with Brent near $105. The TLT short stays at its trimmed 10% because the trend is intact but the yield spike may be exhausting. Web-search coverage of the 10-05 to 10-09 week was sparse, so this decision rests mainly on measured price momentum, not on news.

positions.thesis: Core AI-semis leadership exposure: SMH is +38% over 6 months and +7.7% over 1 month, the strongest trend in the measured universe. The -4.3% week is a pullback inside an uptrend, not a trend break. Kept at 30% as the book's anchor, with a 15% stop as the trend-failure line.

Semicap leader: +27% over 6 months and +11.7% over 1 month despite a sharp September drawdown. The leg is -6.5%, well inside the 15% stop. Held at 10% as the higher-beta capex expression of the AI build-out, with the stop unchanged.

Replaces AVGO at the same 8%. NVDA is +21.6% over 6 months and +12.7% over 3 months, a confirmed leader, while AVGO is negative on both lookbacks. This keeps a single-name AI-compute sleeve without holding a laggard. The overlap with SMH (where NVDA is about 21% of the fund) is accepted because this is a momentum book.

AI power-infrastructure leg: momentum has been flat over 6 months (+1.4%) but has rebounded 8.7% over 1 month, and the leg is +1.5% since entry. Held at a modest 7% under probation with a wide 18% stop because of its volatility, and will be cut next week if the 3-month trend does not turn positive.

Oil-shock E&P leadership: +15.9% over 3 months and +13.7% over 6 months, with Brent around $105. The leg is +2.2%. Held at 15% as the book's second leadership complex and an inflation hedge for the rest of the book.

Long duration is a measured loser: TLT is -9.8% over 6 months and -7.1% over 3 months as the 10y made a 24-year high of 5.34% on 10-05. Kept at the trimmed 10% with a tight 8% stop because yields eased late in the week and a squeeze in this crowded short is the main risk.

Homebuilders are the cleanest equity loser: ITB is -12% over 3 months and -10.1% over 6 months, with mortgage rates pinned by a 5%+ 10-year. The leg is +1%. Held at 12% as the rate-sensitive equity short paired with the long leadership sleeves.
